articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft patches a whopping 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. AI is apparently getting scary good at finding our coding mistakes — better hope it stays on our side.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas education platform gets pwned hard, disrupting schools nationwide with ransom demands plastered on login pages. Nothing says 'back to school' like cybercriminals holding your coursework hostage.

articles.title: How AI Hallucinations Are Creating Real Security Risks
articles.summary: PraisonAI CVE-2026-44338 gets exploited within 4 hours of disclosure because threat actors apparently have better patch management than most enterprises. The irony of an AI orchestration framework getting orchestrated is *chef's kiss*.

articles.title: New Fragnesia Linux Kernel LPE Grants Root Access via Page Cache Corruption
articles.summary: Anonymous researcher drops two more Windows zero-days: BitLocker bypass and CTFMON privilege escalation dubbed 'YellowKey'. Microsoft's having quite the year for unplanned transparency.

articles.title: 18-Year-Old NGINX Rewrite Module Flaw Enables Unauthenticated RCE
articles.summary: Meet 'Fragnesia' — the third Linux kernel LPE in two weeks that grants instant root via page cache corruption. The kernel team might want to consider a career change at this rate.

articles.title: 73 Seconds to Breach, 24 Hours to Patch: The Case for Autonomous Validation
articles.summary: 18-year-old NGINX heap buffer overflow finally discovered — apparently some bugs age like fine wine. CVE-2026-42 proves that sometimes the old vulnerabilities are the most dangerous.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its barely-used end-to-end encryption feature, breaking years-old promises to users. Meta continues its proud tradition of prioritizing ad revenue over actual privacy.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Finally! Apple and Android enable E2E encryption for RCS cross-platform messaging. Only took them forever to stop letting carriers read our texts like digital postcards.

articles.title: AI Drives Cybersecurity Investments, Widening 'Valley of Death'
articles.summary: EFF launches campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, who's been contributing since age 12. Authoritarian regimes really hate people who make information free and accessible.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft in 2022 SMS phishing spree. Another young talent choosing the dark side when they could've been legendary white hats.
